The **geography of [New York City](New_York_City "New York City")** is characterized by its coastal position at the meeting of the [Hudson River](Hudson_River "Hudson River") and the [Atlantic Ocean](Atlantic_Ocean "Atlantic Ocean") in a naturally sheltered [harbor](New_York_Harbor "New York Harbor"). The city's geography, with its scarce availability of land, is a contributing factor in making New York the most densely populated major city in the [United States](United_States "United States"). Environmental issues are chiefly concerned with managing this density, which also explains why New York is among the most energy-efficient and least automobile-dependent cities in the United States. The city's climate is temperate.

## Geography

New York City is located on the coast of the [Northeastern United States](Northeastern_United_States "Northeastern United States") at the mouth of the [Hudson River](Hudson_River "Hudson River") in southeastern [New York](New_York_(state) "New York (state)") state. It is located in the [New York–New Jersey Harbor Estuary](Geography_of_New_York%E2%80%93New_Jersey_Harbor_Estuary "Geography of New York–New Jersey Harbor Estuary"), the centerpiece of which is the [New York Harbor](New_York_Harbor "New York Harbor"), whose deep waters and sheltered bays helped the city grow in significance as a trading city. Much of New York is built on the three islands of Manhattan, Staten Island, and western Long Island, making land scarce and encouraging a high population density.

The Hudson River flows from the [Hudson Valley](Hudson_Valley "Hudson Valley") into [New York Bay](New_York_Bay "New York Bay"), becoming a [tidal estuary](Tidal_estuary "Tidal estuary") that separates the Bronx and Manhattan from Northern New Jersey. The [Harlem River](Harlem_River "Harlem River"), another [tidal strait](Tidal_strait "Tidal strait") between the East and Hudson Rivers, separates Manhattan from the Bronx.

The city's land has been altered considerably by human intervention, with substantial [land reclamation](Land_reclamation "Land reclamation") along the waterfronts since Dutch colonial times. Reclamation is most notable in [Lower Manhattan](Lower_Manhattan "Lower Manhattan") with modern developments like [Battery Park City](Battery_Park_City "Battery Park City"). The **Boroughs of New York City** are the five major governmental districts that compose [New York City](New_York_City "New York City"). The boroughs are [the Bronx](The_Bronx "The Bronx"), <Brooklyn>, <Manhattan>, <Queens>, and [Staten Island](Staten_Island "Staten Island"). Each borough is coextensive with a respective [county](Administrative_divisions_of_New_York_(state)#County "Administrative divisions of New York (state)") of the [State of New York](New_York_(state) "New York (state)"): The Bronx is Bronx County, Brooklyn is Kings County, Manhattan is New York County, Queens is Queens County, and Staten Island is Richmond County.

All five boroughs came into existence with the creation of [modern New York City](City_of_Greater_New_York "City of Greater New York") in 1898, when New York County (then including the Bronx), Kings County, Richmond County, and part of Queens County were consolidated within one municipal government under a [new city charter](New_York_City_Charter "New York City Charter"). All former municipalities within the newly consolidated city were eliminated.

New York City was originally confined to Manhattan Island and the smaller surrounding islands that formed New York County. As the city grew northward, it began annexing areas on the mainland, absorbing territory from [Westchester County](Westchester_County%2C_New_York "Westchester County, New York") into New York County in 1874 ([West Bronx](West_Bronx "West Bronx")) and 1895 ([East Bronx](East_Bronx "East Bronx")). During the 1898 consolidation, this territory was organized as the Borough of the Bronx, though still part of New York County. In 1914, Bronx County was split off from New York County so that each borough was then coterminous with a county.

When the western part of Queens County was consolidated with New York City in 1898, that area became the Borough of Queens. In 1899, the remaining eastern section of Queens County was split off to form [Nassau County](Nassau_County%2C_New_York "Nassau County, New York") on [Long Island](Long_Island "Long Island"), thereafter making the borough and county of Queens coextensive with each other.
